subject: Privacy follow-up: controller/processor roles, subprocessors, and notify timeline
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@healthsync.com>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@healthsync.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from demo — quick privacy questions

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the throughput numbers looked promising. Before our procurement and security teams proceed I'd like to confirm a few data handling items so we can scope the internal approval: 

1) Controller vs. processor: can you confirm Redwood's standard stance in the Privacy Addendum (are we controller or processor for telemetry/LLM inputs)? We need the explicit language for our legal team.
2) Subprocessors: will you provide a current list and what notice (if any) we get for subprocessor changes? Do you offer an option for prior written notice or a right to object for critical subprocessors?
3) Breach notification timing: what is Redwood's SLA for notifying customers if their data is impacted (e.g., confirmed security incident affecting PII)?
4) Data residency: we need an option to keep HealthSync EU-origin data in EU regions — is that available, and is it a separate deployment/contract?
5) Logging and retention: default retention for access logs, request/response logs, and any ability to configure shorter retention.

If you can send the current DPA (or a redline) and a simple dataflow diagram that shows what you store vs. what is ephemeral, that would expedite our procurement review.

Thanks,
Ellen
Ellen Park
Head of Security & Privacy
HealthSync
ellen.park@healthsync.com

Note: procurement@healthsync.com included for visibility; they'll coordinate purchasing questions once we lock the terms.

From: sean.gallagher@redwood.com <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@healthsync.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, mina.haddad@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — quick privacy questions

Hi Ellen — great questions and thanks for the clear list. Short answers here, Mina (cc) will follow up with the technical details and the DPA attachments. Proposed next steps at the bottom.

1) Controller vs Processor: Redwood acts as a processor for customer-supplied prompt/content and as a controller for telemetry/operational metrics we collect for service health. We include the explicit language in the DPA we attach.

2) Subprocessors: we publish the current subprocessor list in the DPA and on our portal. For material changes we notify customers in advance where practicable; for critical third-party security incidents we commit to immediate notification. If you have a strict prior-approval requirement we can discuss a contractual carve-out (typical enterprise addendum).

3) Breach notification timing: our standard commitment is to notify affected customers within 72 hours of confirming an incident that materially affects their data. We will also provide ongoing status updates until the issue is resolved.

4) Data residency: we support region-restricted deployments (hosted EU region or a Dedicated/Private deployment in a customer VPC). There is a configuration/contracting step — I'll include options in the DPA.

5) Logging & retention: default request/trace logs retained 90 days; enterprise plans can extend retention to 365 days. We also offer shorter retention on a per-account basis (can redact or truncate request bodies on ingestion).

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf (DPA draft) and DataFlowDiagram.png (high-level).

Next steps: 
- Mina to send a short technical appendix and the official subprocessor list.
- I'll share a DocuSign link if you want the standard DPA executed; otherwise we can accept redlines and circulate.
- Propose a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk your procurement/security teams through the DPA. What time works for you?

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@healthsync.com>
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — quick privacy questions (technical appendix)

Hi Ellen — following up with the technical details Sean summarized. Happy to set up a technical call if helpful.

- Data retention: default request/response logs and debug traces retained for 90 days. On enterprise contracts we can extend retention up to 365 days or provide a custom retention policy. For scenarios requiring minimal footprint we can enable truncated logging and prompt redaction at ingestion.

- KV cache & ephemeral state: runtime KV caches are memory-resident and not persisted to long-term storage by default. We persist checkpoints for model serving (encrypted) for operational continuity; those do not contain full request bodies.

- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest (customer-managed KMS is available for Private/Dedicated customers).

- Audit & access logs: we provide per-account access logs (API key, timestamp, endpoint). Default retention is 90 days; we can push to your SIEM or a customer-owned S3 for longer retention if required.

- Subprocessor list & change notifications: current list included in the DPA appendix. For routine additions we aim to notify customers via the portal and email at least 30 days in advance when feasible. In case of a security incident at a subprocessor that impacts customer data we will notify immediately and provide remediation steps.

- Incident handling & breach notice: Redwood maintains an incident response plan. For confirmed incidents impacting customer data we notify customers within 72 hours with an initial assessment; a fuller incident report follows as investigations conclude. If you require a shorter SLA we can evaluate it under an enterprise addendum.

- Compliance artifacts: we can share SOC 2 Type II summary/report and an encryption attestation via a secure link after an NDA or MSA if needed.

If you want any of these points tightened into contract language, tell me which items to prioritize and we will draft specific clauses for review.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Director, Security & Privacy Operations | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

(Attachment stubs: Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf [application/pdf], DataFlowDiagram.png [image/png])
